newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up, awaits corporate buying.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up, awaits corporate buying.

text.p: The won closed higher versus the dollar on Wednesday in cautious trading as banks refrained from selling and waited anxiously for companies to start buying the domestic currency, traders said.
Banks had been selling the local currency aggressively in the past couple of days, pushing the won down to an all-time low.
The won closed at 828.40 after opening at 829.00. It fluctuated in a range of 827.80 to 829.30.
"The market is waiting for companies to cash in their export deals prior to Chusok," said a local bank dealer.
Corporate cash demand is usually strong prior to Chusok, Korea's Thanksgiving holiday between September 26-29, because companies pay worker bonuses.
Traders said intervention worries also supported the local currency.
"The central bank is expected to step in if the dollar rises near 830 won," said another dealer.
Dealers expect the won to move in a range of 827.50 to 829.50 on Thursday with a base mid-rate of 828.50. Today's mid-rate was pegged at 828.60.
